title: fix(plugin-auth): a refused OAuth application registration answers the status the refusal declared, not 500
body:
Part of #24773 — this PR does the first half only: a refused registration now answers 4xx instead of 500. The second half, whether a `web` client may register an `http://localhost` / `http://127.0.0.1` redirect URI, is an authentication-flow acceptance rule. It was measured here and nothing about it changed. It goes to a decision card. #24773 remains open.

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`POST /api/v1/auth/sys-oauth-application/register` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`) answered most refusals from better-auth as `500 OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED`.

- **Mechanism, measured against the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.3` / `better-call@1.4.0`.** Every refusal better-auth raises is better-call's `APIError`. It carries its status twice: as the number `statusCode` (`400`) and as the name `status` (`'BAD_REQUEST'`). The door read only a numeric `status`, so every refusal with a named status fell through to `500`. The body-schema `ValidationError` has the number `400` in its `status`, so that refusal answered `400` from the same door. One door gave two answers for the same class of refusal.
- **Fix.** The door now reads the status through `resolveThrownHttpError` (`@objectstack/types`). That is the repo's one rule for which status a thrown error declares: a numeric `status`, then `statusCode`, and the caller's fallback (`500`) when the throw declares neither. The code stays `OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED` (already in the ledger; no new code). `details.upstreamError` still carries the vendor's discriminator.
- **Effect, measured on the real stack.** `web` + `http://localhost:4001/callback` or `http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback`: `500` → `400` (`invalid_redirect_uri`). No session: `500` → `401`. A storage fault while persisting the client: still `500`. Body-schema refusal (`http://app.example.com/callback`): still `400`. `https://app.example.com/callback`: still `200`.

## Tests

New `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-register-refusal-status.test.ts`. It runs real better-auth with the OIDC provider on, behind the plugin's real route registration on a real Hono app, using the `in-process-session-renewal.pin.test.ts` harness. Each refusal asserts the ADR-0112 envelope (`code` + `status`) and `details.upstreamError` where the vendor sends one, and asserts that no `sys_oauth_application` row was written.

- A precondition asserts that the fixture's refusal is a **named-status** `APIError` (`status: 'BAD_REQUEST'`, `statusCode: 400`). If the vendor ever switched to a numeric `status`, the pins below would pass on the old door too, and this precondition says so.
- **Ablation, leg 1** (put the old read back: `const status = typeof err?.status === 'number' ? err.status : 500;`). The mutation was applied with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which confirmed it on disk (anchor 1 → 0, replacement 0 → 1, blob `03e026dea` → `a6bb1a7f3`). Result: `Tests 3 failed | 14 passed (17)`. The failures were `expected 500 to be 400` (localhost), `expected 500 to be 400` (127.0.0.1) and `expected 500 to be 401` (no session). Restored: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Ablation, leg 2** (unknown throw falls back to 400: `resolveThrownHttpError(err, 400)`). Disk-verified the same way (blob `03e026dea` → `16aa6cab0`). Result: `Tests 1 failed | 16 passed (17)` with `expected 400 to be 500` on the storage-fault case. Restored the same way.
- Both legs went red in the direction predicted and nothing else moved. Both ran on head `5dc8add4f`, the commit that carries the fix. The merge of `main` that followed left both files byte-identical (blobs `03e026dea` and `8b2336493`).

**Head `622e30aa9`** is the merge of `main` at `5cb6e6e0a`. The incoming commits touch none of this diff's files, and `packages/spec` `check:generated` is all up to date after the rebuild. On that head:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run`: `Test Files 169 passed (169)`, `Tests 3241 passed | 10 skipped (3251)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0, with `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- The derived local gate union (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 72 commands) ran with every exit code captured before any pipe: 72 of 72 exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation printed `72 derived, 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.

## Half 2 — measured, not changed (for the decision card)

- **The vendor's predicate.** This is `validateClientRedirectUri`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.3`. A `web` client is refused unless the URI is `https:` **and** the host is not loopback (`localhost` or a loopback IP). The message "web clients require https redirect URIs on non-loopback hosts" states that conjunction. It does not exempt loopback hosts. Measured through this door, every loopback form is refused for `web`: `http://localhost`, `http://localhost:4001`, `http://127.0.0.1:4001`, `http://[::1]:4001`, and also `https://localhost` and `https://127.0.0.1`. Port and IP family make no difference. A `native` client may use `http` on exactly `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, with any port. Called directly with `application_type: 'native'`, the vendor accepted `http://localhost:4001/callback` and `http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback`. The predicate takes no options, so no configuration plugin-auth passes (trusted origins, dev mode, dynamic client registration) governs it.
- **The door drops the Console's Application Type.** The form's `type` select (web / native / user-agent-based) is forwarded as the body key `type`. The installed vendor's `/oauth2/create-client` body schema declares no `type`. It declares `application_type: 'web' | 'native'`. So the key is stripped, and every registration is judged and stored as `web`. Measured: `type: 'native'` + `http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback` is refused with the web rule. `type: 'native'` + an `https` URI is stored with `application_type: "web"`.
- **The field help.** "One URL per line. Must use https:// in production." (`packages/platform-objects`, `sys_oauth_application` create action) does not match the measured rule for `web`: https always, never a loopback host.

The options, analysed on the four axes, are in the dev report on the card. This PR changes none of them.

## Acceptance notes

- Not changed here, and noted without a card: on a server fault the door answers with the thrown error's raw `message` (in the test, `storage fault (test)`) and logs nothing on that branch. This is the existing behaviour and out of this card's scope.
- `test:repo` (vitest `repo` project) was not run locally; it is CI's (`Test Core`).
